mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the discount rate for future cash flows declines, lowering the present value of expected dividends and thereby pushing S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during the period of below-average FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) reduce consumer and business confidence, lowering expected corporate earnings growth and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above the 4.0% level observed at t-1mo
failure_condition: 20-day and 60-day forward returns are both positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the post-unemployment-rising period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening domestic demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO exceeds its prior month's level by at least 2.0 percentage points
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the INDPRO surge.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% suggests the Fed may hold rates steady longer, reducing discount rate expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns up over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative with a p-value > 0.05 during periods of sub-3% CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the S&P 500 20-day forward return indicate a countercyclical relationship; however, a sharp rise in the S&P 500 20-day forward return after a dual drop in UNRATE and HOUST (industrial production) suggests a reversal, predicting positive returns over the next 20 days when both UNRATE and HOUST fall then rebound.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and HOUST both fall for two consecutive months, then HOUST recovers in the third month
regime_hint: Reversal from labor market weakness to strength
failure_condition: No significant return reversal detected in walk-forward tests across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed expectations by more than 10% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4%, it signals a robust labor market that boosts corporate optimism, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during qualifying payrolls events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales proxy (not available in the given catalog; fallback: use HOUST as a demand proxy) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests shifting consumer versus business demand, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by >2% month-over-month
regime_hint: Demand reallocation from industry to retail
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such demand shifts.

mechanism_narrative: During a sharp rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5%, the anticipation of tighter financing conditions compresses growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a sustained manner
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or are only marginally negative with p-value > 0.10 during tightening periods.
